belief: I am saved by my good works.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you are saved by your good works, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Believing that good people go to heaven and bad people do not. Being taught that church attendance, giving, or service earns God’s favor. A home where love was earned by performance. Comparing yourself with others who seem worse. Never clearly hearing the gospel of grace.
teaches: Salvation is a gift of God’s grace received through faith in Jesus, not a reward for good works. God saved us not because of righteous things we had done, but because of His mercy. No one is justified by keeping rules. Good works still matter: we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works. But they are the fruit of salvation, not the root of it.
self_statements: I’m a good person, so God will accept me.
If my good deeds outweigh my bad ones, I’ll be fine.
I have to keep doing more to be saved.
God owes me for all I’ve done.
I’m better than most people, so I’m safe.
If I stop serving, I’ll lose my salvation.
errors: Measuring yourself against other people instead of God’s holiness.
Treating salvation like a balance of good and bad deeds.
Believing your goodness earns God’s acceptance.
Working harder out of fear rather than gratitude.
questions: What does Ephesians 2:8–9 say salvation is: a wage or a gift?
How many good works would be enough to make up for one sin?
If I could earn salvation, why did Jesus need to die?
Am I comparing myself to people or to God’s holiness?
Do I serve God out of love, or to keep my place with Him?
What does Ephesians 2:10 say good works are for?
Have I ever simply received Christ as my Savior?
truth: I am not saved by my good works. I am saved by God’s grace through faith in Jesus Christ. Salvation is a gift, not something I earn. Because I am saved, I want to do good works out of gratitude and love, as God’s workmanship in Christ.
hw_questions: Is salvation a wage or a gift?
How many good deeds would make up for one sin?
If I could earn it, why did Jesus die?
Am I comparing myself to people or to God?
Do I serve from love or from fear?
hw_truths: I am saved by grace through faith.
Salvation is God’s gift, not my wage.
God saved me because of His mercy.
Good works are the fruit of salvation, not the root.
I serve God out of gratitude, not to earn His love.
I am God’s workmanship in Christ.
log: Each day, write one thing I did for God, then write: “Not to earn, but because I am loved.”
name_example: For it is by grace Sarah has been saved through faith, and this not from herself; it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast.
actions: Write down every good thing you hope will get you to heaven,
then write across it: “Saved by grace, through faith, as a gift.”
Pray a simple prayer receiving Christ as your Savior,
or thanking Him again if you already have.
Do one good deed in secret this week
purely out of thanks to God, and tell no one.
and write in your own words how a person is made right with God.
tracker: One good deed done from gratitude
prayer: Father, thank You that salvation is Your free gift through Jesus Christ. Help me reject the lie that I am saved by my good works. I trust in Christ alone. Let my good works flow from gratitude, not fear, as I live as Your workmanship. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: The refrain says Jesus paid it all, so there is nothing left for my good works to pay.
Salvation is pictured as a gift that sets us free, not a wage we earn.
Asks what can wash away sin and answers: nothing but the blood of Jesus.
Not What My Hands Have Done
Names what our own efforts cannot do and points to Christ alone.
